tagline: Back roads of Southern Maryland, from church to colonial church.
intro: The byway starts at Port Tobacco and wanders down across Charles and St. Mary's counties on tree-lined back roads through farmland, over Zekiah Swamp and by the old port of Chaptico to Leonardtown, then down MD 5 to Point Lookout, where a Civil War prison camp stood at the tip of land between the Potomac and the Chesapeake.

The colony's first settlement was founded as a haven for Catholics and Protestants alike, and the churches came early. St. Ignatius, founded by the Jesuits in 1641, is the oldest continuously serving Catholic parish in the nation, and St. George's at Valley Lee has held services since 1638.

moments.title: Port Tobacco
moments.text: Once the second-largest town in Maryland, until the river silted up and the railroad passed it by. It now counts 18 residents, the smallest incorporated town in the state.

moments.title: St. Clement's Island
moments.text: Off Coltons Point lies the island where Father Andrew White said the first Catholic Mass in the British American colonies, in 1634.

moments.title: Historic St. Mary's City
moments.text: Maryland's capital from 1634 to 1695, rebuilt as a living-history town, with a replica of the Dove, one of the two ships that brought the first settlers.
